title: Windows process-tree stop never kills unrelated processes through reused parent PIDs
user_story: As a researcher pressing Stop (and as the CI owner) I need cancellation to stop only the processes my run started; Windows PID reuse must never let it kill unrelated programs or the CI runner.

requirements.description: A process is a descendant only if its ParentProcessId names a tree member AND it was created no earlier than that member; termination uses the same handle that was checked.
CLI, sandbox, remote launcher and CI repair cancellation never use taskkill /T; the remote launcher stays free of backend imports.
If the tree stop fails, the owned process is still killed through its own handle; completion is reported only by the waiter.

nonfunctional: No new runtime dependency (ctypes only in backend)
No test, assertion or threshold relaxed
preconditions: Windows host for the real-process scenario
acceptance_criteria: Real owned tree stopped while a bystander survives

scenarios.expected: Older processes naming a reused parent PID are excluded with their subtree
Denied tree stop still kills the owned process once
Real tree stop completes within the 10 s owned wait

recovery: Revert processes.py and the four call sites. TASK-CI-WIN-HANG-6513 (owner-authorized root-cause fix 2026-10-27).
test_environment: Real processes on every platform (owned stop + bystander survival); grandchild tree stop asserted on Windows, where the identity-checked walk applies; deterministic snapshot selection everywhere.

review.method: Same-agent review (not independent): creation-time rule per edge, handle reuse between check and kill, launcher independence, double-kill avoidance.

tdd.scope: RED: before the fix (no select_descendants/stop_tree): 5/5 ERROR. GREEN: with the fix: 5/5 PASS. Two older taskkill-specific tests (test_process_stop, test_provider_connectivity) were updated to the replaced mechanism.
